rationale: This is a cosmetic rescaling of the archive's best performer ("R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover", fmb 4.15/talpha 3.52) — swapping the denominator from total liabilities to current liabilities plus a small xrd term leaves the same economic construct and highly correlated rank ordering, so it tests denominator sensitivity rather than a new mechanism.

The expression is internally consistent with the stated negative sign and the R&D-addback loss *level* is a substantively different second leg from the archive's gross-margin-deterioration spiral, though it recombines two already-tested channels (addback profitability, liability growth) and inherits the earlier spiral's risk of a strong FMB slope with negligible portfolio alpha.

This is a direct rediscovery of the archived "Internal-Knowledge Solvency Mix" with the only change being SUB of two raw ratios replaced by SUMRANK of the same two ratios — a pure normalization tweak, not a new hypothesis.

The goodwill-share-of-equity-cushion construct is a genuinely different framing from the archive's gdwl/at scalings and pairs coherently with cash burn, but the ratio gdwl/(gdwl+ceq) is non-monotonic and sign-flipping when ceq is negative — exactly the distressed population targeted — so winsorization alone will not prevent the most fragile firms from landing in the wrong tail.

This is a mechanical transplant that bolts the first leg of "Liquidity-Forced R&D Retrenchment" (retrenchment in intangible spending) onto the *identical* second leg of "Advertising Liquidity Squeeze" ((lct−che)/at), at ~4–5% coverage, so it is a recombination of tested parts rather than a new mechanism.

It is close to the sign-mirror of the already-tested "R&D Liquidity Repair Reinvestment" (which failed on the portfolio leg), the interaction_type field is blank, and the core interaction is partly mechanical since higher cash R&D spending directly reduces working capital — so a hit would be hard to distinguish from an accounting identity.
